raw_response:
I have only 4.1 mu, so I will count every bag and every trip to the field. What I do always starts from what worked before, and I do not like taking big chances. Cotton is still the crop I trust most, so I will keep the biggest piece for cotton, then leave a smaller piece for wheat and maize. I have a well, so I will use water when the field really needs it, because if I save too much on water and fertilizer and the crop goes weak, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. For fertilizer, I will not do fancy things. I will put enough base fertilizer in the ground, then topdress again when the crop is growing strong. Cotton eats longer, so I will feed it a bit heavier and water it more times. Wheat I will keep steady, like most people around here do, because wheat must not start weak. Maize grows fast in summer, so I will give it a good first dose and one chase fertilizer later. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen other people get better stands and fuller bolls or ears, but I will not chase expensive new things just to try them. I do most work with family labor, so I will keep the plan simple enough that I can finish it on time.
